history.new: Computing the row at time t of an affine magma automaton by binary exponentiation of P = a + bS modulo S^L - 1 (FFT products) is exact and, at L = 1024, faster than direct numpy simulation by about one order of magnitude at t = 10^3, two orders at 10^4 (138-314x in two runs) and three orders at 10^5 (1,459-2,500x); t = 10^9 takes milliseconds for L <= 4096. With the same timing protocol on both sides it loses for t below about 20.
history.old: Computing the row at time t of an affine magma automaton by binary exponentiation of P = a + bS modulo S^L - 1 (FFT products) is exact and, at L = 1024, about 3-4x faster than direct numpy simulation at t = 100, 22-29x at 10^3, 138-215x at 10^4 and 1800-2500x at 10^5; t = 10^9 takes 1.5-8 ms for L <= 4096.
